title: Khao Man Gai
subtitle: Thai poached chicken with ginger-infused rice
excerpt: A whole chicken is gently poached in water with ginger and garlic, and the rice is cooked in the resulting broth. Simple and clean, with a punchy dipping sauce alongside.
sourceNotes: Khao man gai is the Thai version of Hainanese chicken rice, which spread across Southeast Asia with Chinese immigration. It is a beloved street food dish across Thailand, served simply with rich broth and a sharp dipping sauce.

content.text: The key is not to boil the chicken. Keep the water at a very gentle simmer the whole time.

items.prepNote: 2 for the broth, 2 sliced for serving

content.text: Put the whole chicken in the stockpot. Cover with cold water.
Add the ginger, garlic, 2 spring onions and a large pinch of salt. Bring slowly to the boil.
As soon as the water boils, reduce to the lowest possible simmer. Cover and cook for 40 minutes.
Remove the chicken. Check it is cooked by piercing the thigh; the juices should run clear.
Ladle 600ml of the hot broth into a separate saucepan. Add the rinsed rice.
Bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat. Leave covered for 5 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, lime juice and chilli for the dipping sauce.
Carve or pull the chicken into pieces. Drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve the chicken on the rice with a small bowl of broth and the dipping sauce alongside. Top with sliced spring onions.

items.symptom: Chicken is still pink near the bone.
items.cause: A larger bird or higher heat needed longer cooking.
items.fix: Return to the simmering broth for 10 more minutes.

items.cause: Too much liquid or lid was lifted during cooking.
items.fix: Keep the lid on throughout; use the exact 600ml ratio.

items.cause: The water was too much for the chicken size.
items.fix: Reduce the remaining broth in the pot for 15 minutes before serving.
